page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 288 virtual CPUs mapped to 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1080 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the server includes 48 local NVMe SSDs totaling 19,031 GB of capacity. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 22,949.13 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 1,062.88 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and PassMark memory scores falling into the middle 50% tier.

Database and web serving operations perform exceptionally well, with Redis SET operations achieving 407.31 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 241.6 GB/sec. Large language model (LLM) prompt processing is strong, but text generation speeds are a notable bottleneck, dropping to the bottom 25% tier for small models and the middle 50% tier for large models. This profile makes the server highly suitable for heavy multi-threaded compute tasks, large-scale database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM text generation.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd is an x86_64 server featuring 288 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor, 1080 GB of RAM, and 19,031 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 48 drives. Operating at 2.3 GHz with a 504 MB L3 cache, it delivers top-tier multi-core CPU and memory read bandwidth performance, placing in the top 10% of benchmarks. While single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are moderate to weak, the server excels in multi-threaded workloads, database operations, and high-throughput web serving. Its high resource density provides qualitative cost efficiency for massive parallel processing and storage-heavy database workloads, offering a powerful balance of compute and local storage without dedicated GPU acceleration. It is highly optimized for enterprise-scale databases, software compilation, and intensive data processing tasks.
